verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input to this bottom-up has been public for two months: the May and June asset splits and net deposits were released 2026-07-07 (TPA $99.1bn, cash $44.8bn, advisory $54.3bn, cash net deposits -$235m), and the 0.58% cash / ~0.21% advisory take rates come from the 2026-06-04 Q1 FY27 release and call. Six to seven sell-side analysts cover the name and have been cutting continuously since the last print -- Goldman to $10.50, KBW $11.00 then $10.50, Wells Fargo $11.50 -- against a January mean target near $16. The stock at $9.655 sits below the lowest of those revised targets and 30.8% below its 52-week high, having fallen on all three prior prints. That is a market that has already stopped believing the vendor consensus line. The genuinely new part is only the *precise* size of the gap, and even that is shaky: the hunter uses 0.58% when the company disclosed a 54bp May-end run rate, so its own $94.5m is internally inconsistent with the disclosure it is built on, and I could not verify that the current Q2 revenue consensus is still $98.0m rather than already marked down. What survives is that consensus of ~$98m implies +8% QoQ off a $90.5m Q1 on roughly flat assets, which the disclosed take rates cannot produce -- that specific arithmetic I found published nowhere.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The company said this itself, on the record, on 2026-06-04. The MarketBeat/TradingView summary of that call states the 58bp fee rate decline was 'driven primarily by the lower Fed funds rate and the company's new cross-product adoption incentive, which affected two months of the quarter' -- the 'two of three months' framing is management's own words, not the hunter's inference. The 25bp Direct-Deposit-Plus-Investing boost with no expiration and no balance cap is on Wealthfront's public product page, and the adoption ladder (61% at FY26 year-end, ~63% by late May) was given on the same call. The only step beyond disclosure is 'therefore three months in Q2 instead of two,' which is arithmetic anyone listening to the call performs. It also runs into a company-supplied ceiling: management put the May-end rate at 54bp but 56bp on an EFFR-neutral basis, i.e. only ~2bp of the 4bp quarterly decline is structural, which caps the incremental Q2 drag at roughly $2m of revenue -- about 2% of the quarter, not a thesis.

The 2026-01-12 EPS beat followed by a -16.84% reaction is in the baseline history and in public estimate tables (Q3 FY26: $0.21 actual vs $0.20 estimate, then -16.8%), and the May-to-June cash net deposit swing to -$235m was in the 2026-07-07 metrics release and was the lead of trade-press coverage ('Wealthfront hits record $99.1 billion in June as advisory inflows offset cash outflows'). verdicts.strongest_argument: This is optics on a number the market has already been shown twice, and its arithmetic base is wrong in the direction that matters. June TPA was $99.1bn and the hunter's own cited source says the S&P was *negative in June and July* -- so the July quarter-end figure, which is the one that anchors the P&L, most likely printed below $99.1bn, and August's +2.7% is climbing back from a lower base rather than adding to $99.1bn. More damaging: the company crossed to record assets in June and the trade press led with it on 2026-07-07, and the last time record assets were reported alongside the P&L (2026-06-04, 'Record Asset Growth Amid Strategic Trade-offs') the stock fell 14.35%. A round-number headline that has demonstrably failed to hold the stock twice is not a catalyst worth more than a point or two. The August market move itself is fully public macro. The only unpriced element is that nobody has published an August TPA estimate for this specific company, which is worth something but not much.

interactions: Three clusters. (1) h1#1 and h2#0 are the same fact from the same document, arrived at separately: both rest on the 2026-06-04 Q1 FY27 call for the Direct-Deposit-Plus take-rate drag, and the convergence is not corroboration because the underlying statement is management's own ('the new cross-product adoption incentive, which affected two months of the quarter'). They should be treated as one ~2bp/$2m-per-quarter item, not two; h2#0 additionally under-weights the company's 56bp EFFR-neutral bridge, which caps the structural portion of the decline. (2) h1#3 and h2#2 are direct mirrors of one identical fact -- the cash-to-advisory migration visible in the 2026-07-07 June metrics. h1#3 reads it as a bullish round-number platform-assets headline; h2#2 reads the same migration as revenue-dilutive at ~60% revenue loss per migrating dollar. They cannot both be scored as edge; they are one observation with a contested sign, and the trade press has published the bullish read (TradeInformer, July 2026) while the bearish read is unpublished. Note also that h1#3's arithmetic base is undermined by its own cited source, which states June and July were negative index months, so July TPA likely printed below the $99.1bn it extrapolates from. (3) h1#2 and h2#4 both rest on the same 2026-08-19 scheduling release for the 'July and August flows both land tonight' mechanism; h2#4 states only the schedule and carries no direction, while h1#2 supplies the directional content. Scoring both credits the same disclosure twice. Finally, h2#3 (bullish, rate regime flipped) and h1#0/h1#2/h2#0/h2#1/h2#2 (bearish) point in opposite directions on the same stock, but they do not actually collide on this print: h2#3's mechanism resolves at the 2026-09-16 FOMC a week after the release and cannot enter the May-July P&L, whereas the bearish cluster is about the quarter being reported.
